Its accepted definition carves it as information that is 'collected, stores, and possesses but cannot access, use, or analyze', and it explicitly distinguishes itself from missing data ('data that does not exist') precisely by being stored-but-inaccessible. Not identity (dark-data is a category of information, not the storage system) and not purpose: a genuine constitutive dependency, analogous to the accepted semitone DEPENDS_ON pitch.

Law 8d (for whose sake?): ZPD's own accepted definition carves it as a construct 'used in educational theory to define the space where learning occurs' — it maps a developmental-capacity space; its master is the learning space it delineates, not the transmission practice. The note's pinned sense overreaches: 'only defined in relation to instructional guidance' is false under the from-side's definition — its parameters (independent level, assisted level, scaffold) are supplied by 'a more knowledgeable person', which includes peers and collaborators, not the teaching institution. Explanatory dependence is not operational dependence (Laws 2b/8b). The note's own load-bearing clause says interleaving would "lose its explanatory mechanism" if cognitive-load-theory were removed — an explanation, not an operation. The technique's operation is behavioral: present mixed problem types, force discrimination, select strategies. It operates in mathematics, music, and sports training (per its accepted definition) with or without anyone knowing Sweller's framework; the technique predates and is independently practiced apart from CLT, and its credited mechanism in its own definition is discrimination and retrieval practice, not load classification. Removing the theory does not stop the practice operating; at most one candidate account of why it works is removed. If anything, the honest relation is DERIVED_FROM-grade (the technique's research literature draws on load theory), not DEPENDS_ON.

A mark is not an instance of its craft (Law 9a: a topic is not an instance of its discipline). Typography's accepted definition carves a CRAFT — "the craft of designing the visual arrangement of written text" with parameters like typeface family, leading, kerning, margin proportions. A diacritic is a mark: its accepted definition carves "a mark or symbol added to a letter or character… a secondary graphic element superimposed on a base glyph." The note even pins the right thing — "a specific kind of TYPGRAPHIC MARK" — and then files the mark against the craft. The nearest accepted kind for the pinned mark-sense is glyph ("a visually distinct character, mark, or symbol that functions as a unit within a writing system"; a combining diacritic is literally a glyph), and diacritic's accepted kind-edge is already seated: diacritic INSTANCE_OF symbol. Filing INSTANCE_OF typography confuses the object with the activity that arranges it.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): "a short, memorable phrase repeated by a character or entity, becoming widely associated with them." Phrase's accepted definition: a group of words forming a single unit of meaning within a larger syntactic structure. A catchphrase is exactly such a unit — its own accepted definition opens "a self-contained linguistic unit — a phrase, clause, or single line — constructed for high memorability and rapid cultural transmission." The defining parameter that distinguishes it (association + repetition + detachable context) is added to the phrase base, not substituted for it. Nearest-kind (Laws 9/11e): idiom is NOT the kind — idiom's carve is semantic opacity (meaning non-compositional), while a catchphrase's meaning is typically compositional ("Bye, Felicia"); idiom is a sibling leaf, not a parent. No other accepted kind sits between; catchphrase's existing accepted edges (INSTANCE_OF language, INSTANCE_OF expression) do not make phrase derivable, and phrase itself sits under the same expression umbrella, so the rung completes the structure rather than leaping it.

The note conflates the bar with the bar LINE (Law 11d sense-pin against the accepted carve). bar's accepted definition carves a UNIT OF MUSICAL TIME: "a unit of musical time… containing exactly the number of beats specified by the time signature. It segments musical rhythm into regularly recurring temporal units, enabling performers to navigate complex rhythms through structural grouping," persisting through "Western music notation conventions, pedagogical practice, and PERFORMANCE TRADITION." Removal test (Law 8b): remove the staff now — does the measure stop operating? No. The measure as a temporal grouping of beats operates in performance (performers count bars with no notation at all), in pedagogy, and in other notations; its operational substrate is the beat and the time signature, not five parallel lines. What genuinely depends on the staff are the MARKS drawn on it — and the board already seats those: barline DEPENDS_ON staff, note DEPENDS_ON staff, rest DEPENDS_ON staff, clef DEPENDS_ON staff, all ACCEPTED. "Beats are positioned relative to staff lines/spaces" is pitch placement, not what makes a bar a bar. The honest dependency is the one already on the board: bar DERIVED_FROM musical-notation.

Part-and-whole (Law 10) in the pinned sense: "beats are literal temporal parts contained within the bar's span." bar's accepted definition states the measure "contains exactly the number of beats specified by the time signature"; beat's accepted definition is "a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis in time, the temporal unit that organizes rhythmic experience" — the metronomic backbone of meter. The measure is the whole composed of its beats as temporal parts (a 4/4 bar's span is constituted by its four beats), and the board already treats the beat as the temporal substrate of this cluster: meter DEPENDS_ON beat is ACCEPTED. Removing the beats would leave the measure an empty span with no constituent units — the whole loses its parts. CONTAINS, whole to part, holds in the pinned sense.

payload.scope: A human-made musical construct: a set of two or more pitches sounded simultaneously, whose members bear harmonic relations to one another, built to persist as a fundamental unit of Western harmony through theoretical analysis, performance practice, notation, and teaching.

payload.body: A chord is a human-made musical construct: a set of two or more pitches (notes) sounded simultaneously, whose members bear harmonic relations to one another. Parameters: (1) size — the number of constituent pitches: dyad (two), triad (three), seventh chord (four), ninth chord (five) and beyond; (2) quality — the intervallic structure among the members: major (root–major third–perfect fifth), minor (root–minor third–perfect fifth), diminished (root–minor third–diminished fifth), augmented (root–major third–augmented fifth); (3) inversion — the arrangement of the members by which a different member occupies the bass position, changing the surface harmony while preserving the chord's identity; (4) voicing — the specific octave placement and spacing of the members, which affects the chord's texture without changing its harmonic function. Persistence mechanism: standardized in Western music theory through harmonic analysis, taught in harmony and ear-training curricula, reproduced in performance practice through chord symbols in lead sheets and jazz charts, and maintained through the notation of figured bass and the modern chord symbol system (e.g., 'Cmaj7', 'Am7b5'). It is distinguished from a single note (which fixes one pitch; the chord fixes a set), from a scale (which organizes pitches sequentially into a framework; the chord presents them simultaneously), and from a melody (which unfolds pitches in time; the chord suspends them together). [formal: chorda | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A tree data structure is a human-made hierarchical data structure: a finite set of nodes in which one distinguished root node has zero or more child nodes, every non-root node has exactly one parent, and no cycle occurs — equivalently, a connected acyclic structure (an arborescence) rooted at the root. Parameters: (1) branching factor — the maximum number of children any node may have, unbounded in the general tree and restricted to two (left and right) in the binary specialization; (2) ordering — whether a node's children carry a left-to-right order (ordered tree) or form an unordered set; (3) labeling — the value, key, or payload attached to nodes; (4) height — the length of the longest root-to-leaf path. Persistence mechanism: specified in algorithm textbooks and formal specifications (the CLRS lineage), implemented in software libraries as node-link or array (heap) representations, and maintained as the canonical form of hierarchical data — database indexes (B-trees in relational engines), file-system hierarchies, document object models, and parse trees in compilers. It is distinguished from a graph (which allows arbitrary edges and cycles; the tree is its connected-acyclic, rooted special case), from a linked list (a single chain — a degenerate tree of branching factor one), and from the English word 'tree' (the lexical item, filed on the board as a WORD-referent entry; this entry is the data structure that word names in one of its senses, and the two persist independently of one another). [formal: arbor structurae | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Priming is a human-made cognitive construct: a psychological effect in which exposure to a stimulus (the prime) systematically influences the response to a subsequent stimulus (the target), independent of conscious awareness or intentional effort. Parameters: (1) prime modality — visual, auditory, semantic, or emotional; (2) prime-target interval — the time between prime exposure and target presentation, typically ranging from milliseconds to hours; (3) prime-target relation — the semantic, perceptual, or associative link that must hold between prime and target for the effect to occur; (4) repetition threshold — the number of prime exposures required to produce a measurable effect, which varies by modality and individual susceptibility. Persistence mechanism: operationalized through controlled experimental paradigms (masked priming, repetition priming, associative priming) in cognitive psychology labs, replicated across laboratories through standardized protocols (e.g., the lexical-decision task, the Stroop paradigm, and the primed naming task), and maintained through the cumulative evidence base reported in peer-reviewed research. It is distinguished from learning (which requires repeated exposure and produces durable change; priming can occur in a single trial), from expectation (which involves conscious prediction; priming operates below awareness), and from mere exposure (which changes preference through familiarity rather than response facilitation). [formal: praeparatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a session | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Law 8d — for whose sake is it built? The catchphrase's accepted definition: 'constructed for high memorability and rapid cultural transmission... a human-made rhetorical technology for encoding a distinctive voice or idea into a form that survives its source.' Encoding and transmission are precisely what communication is, per its accepted definition: 'the intentional exchange of meaning through encoded signals.' A catchphrase is an encoding technology — it exists to carry a voice or idea into other minds efficiently, and its persistence mechanism is repetition 'in speech, quotation, and parody across audiences.' Remove communication and the catchphrase is a stored string with no office. The pinned sense ('designed to convey meaning efficiently and persist across repeated use') is the communication sense. Communication is a well-populated beneficiary shelf (acronym, initialism, metaphor, quotation, tact all stand beneath it); a catchphrase is the same kind of servant — a compact carrier of meaning.

Law 8d — for whose sake is it built? A diacritic, per its accepted definition, is a mark 'added to a letter or character to indicate pronunciation, modify meaning, or distinguish it from another form within a writing system,' encoding 'a phonological, orthographic, or semantic distinction that the base alphabet alone cannot express.' Orthography, per its accepted definition, is exactly that base system: 'a standardized system of written conventions' with a grapheme inventory and phoneme-to-grapheme mapping rules, stabilized by authority. Diacritics are the disambiguation mechanism the orthographic system depends on — the definition's own examples are orthographic distinctions (mal vs. mal, nai've vs. naive), and its persistence is through 'typographic conventions, orthographic codes, and digital encoding standards.' Built for the sake of orthographic precision: a diacritic with no orthographic code to serve is a stray mark. The pinned sense ('to indicate pronunciation, tone, or distinction within a writing system... to serve orthographic clarity') is the orthography sense. Complementary accepted edges confirm the structure: diacritic DEPENDS_ON writing, orthography INSTANCE_OF writing — the mark serves the convention system within the shared substrate.

Law 9a: a topic is not an instance of its discipline. The accepted definition of pedagogy carves 'the systematic practice and study of methods and techniques for teaching and instruction' — a domain of crafted frameworks, methodologies, and institutionalized approaches. The accepted definition of ZPD carves 'a psychological construct used in educational theory to define the space where learning occurs' — a diagnostic region: the gap between independent and assisted performance. A competent speaker calls ZPD 'a concept from developmental psychology used in education,' not 'a pedagogy.' Compare the accepted children on this same shelf: scaffolding is a technique deployed in a classroom; worked-examples are an instructional aid presented to a learner. ZPD is not something a teacher deploys — it is something a teacher measures against, and then deploys scaffolding within. The construct is the object the discipline studies and the methods target; it is not a method, technique, or framework of instruction itself. The pinned sense concedes the point by calling ZPD 'a pedagogical concept' — a concept about pedagogy is a topic within it, and Law 9a files no edge for that. (No closer accepted kind exists for ZPD on the board — that is a gap the frontier can fill, not a reason to seat it on the wrong shelf.)

replacementSpec.scopeJustification: A beat is the human-made temporal unit of rhythmic experience: a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis that organizes music, poetry, and movement into patterned, countable units. It is built to persist as the metronomic backbone of meter and prosody — maintained through notation, performance practice, pedagogy, and the human capacity to track and coordinate to regular intervals.
replacementSpec.definitionBody: A beat is a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis in time, the temporal unit that organizes rhythmic experience in music, poetry, and movement. It is the measured interval between successive accents that structures temporal perception into patterned units — the metronomic backbone of musical meter and the stress alternations that govern prosodic rhythm in verse. A beat does not require sound: it operates as an abstract temporal scaffold that can be realized through sound, gesture, speech, or even imagined internally, but its persistence mechanism is the human capacity to track regular intervals and to coordinate action to them. The beat is the map of temporal regularity that humans impose on flowing time, enabling synchronization across bodies and between body and artifact.[formal: pulsus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.note: Removal test (Law 8b): remove the interval construct — the named, categorized distance between two pitches per its accepted definition — and chord stops operating as a unit of harmonic analysis. Chord's own accepted definition fixes its quality parameter in interval terms: major (root–major third–perfect fifth), minor (root–minor third–perfect fifth), diminished, augmented. Without the interval construct a chord is an undifferentiated mass of simultaneous pitches: major and minor can no longer be told apart, chord symbols can no longer be read, and harmonic analysis — the mechanism by which chord persists (theory, notation, pedagogy) — has nothing to name. A chord's identity is fixed by the intervallic structure among its members, so the dependency is operational, not mere sayability. Pinned sense: chord as a harmonic unit whose quality is determined by intervals, not chord as a bare simultaneous set of pitches.

Removal test (Law 8b): remove the semitone construct and equal-temperament stops operating. Its accepted definition IS 'the convention dividing the octave into twelve equal semitones' — the semitone is the unit the octave is divided into, and the 'equal' that names the system is the equality of those twelve semitone steps. Without the semitone construct there is no unit to divide the octave into, no way to state the equal spacing that defines the tuning, and no way to specify its consequences: the keyboard layout (adjacent keys one semitone apart) and the twelve equal keys it makes playable are both stated in semitone terms. The dependency is definitional-operational, not chronology and not mere sayability. Pinned sense: equal-temperament as the twelve-equal-semitone division of the octave.

payload.reasoning: Removal test runs on the DEFINED sense. Chord's accepted definition builds it out of PITCH: 'a set of two or more pitches (notes) sounded simultaneously.' Interval is not a constitutive input of that definition — it is structure AMONG the chord's own members (parameter 2: 'quality — the intervallic structure among the members'), i.e. derived from the chord's pitches, not a substrate the chord is built from. Remove the interval construct now: the set of simultaneous pitches still sounds, is still performed, is still counted in practice; major/minor differences survive as actual audible pitch relations. What is lost is naming and classification — an appeal to language, not operation (Law 8b): 'chord symbols can no longer be read' and 'harmonic analysis has nothing to name' are precisely the naming-consequences that, standing alone, file no dependency. Direction is if anything reversed: intervals among a chord's members are downstream of the chord, and both chord and interval take pitch as substrate — the board has already accepted interval DEPENDS_ON pitch. Pinned sense (Law 11d): chord as simultaneous pitch set per its accepted definition, quality as a derived parameter.

Equal-temperament's accepted definition fixes its constitutive input: parameter (1) 'frame — the octave, the 2:1 frequency ratio being divided', and the board already accepted equal-temperament DEPENDS_ON octave on exactly that ground. The definition supplies its own unit — 'twelve equal steps, each step carrying a frequency ratio of 2^(1/12) ... exactly 100 cents' — so 'there is no unit to divide the octave into' is false: the equal spacing is stated as 2^(1/12) per step, not via the semitone construct. 'Semitone' appears in the definition as a gloss naming the RESULTING step ('each step (the chromatic semitone)') — output of the division, not input. Remove the semitone construct now: the convention (divide the octave into twelve equal 2^(1/12) steps) still operates — specified, manufactured (twelve keys per octave), standardized (A4=440 on 100-cent steps), notated; what is lost is the name, not the system. And the semitone's own accepted definition cannot be a constitutive input without circularity: its size is defined as a function of tuning ('exactly 100 in equal temperament, roughly 112 diatonic and roughly 90 chromatic in just intonation') — so its 100-cent size in equal temperament is DERIVED FROM equal temperament, while the construct spans tunings that have no equal temperament at all. Pinned sense (Law 11d): equal-temperament as the mathematical division convention per its accepted definition.

A beat does not require sound: it operates as an abstract temporal scaffold that can be realized through sound, gesture, speech, or even imagined internally, but its persistence mechanism is the human capacity to track regular intervals and to coordinate action to them. The beat is the map of temporal regularity that humans impose on flowing time, enabling synchronization across bodies and between body and artifact.[formal: pulsus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: interference-beat
payload.scope: The human-made measurement technique that exploits the periodic amplitude modulation produced when two waves of slightly different frequencies superpose. The construct is the map — naming, quantifying, and exploiting this natural interference to reveal the frequency difference between two sources — not the interference itself. Distinct from the musical beat (the rhythmic pulse that organizes meter and serves rhythm): this is an interference measure, not a temporal unit of emphasis.

payload.body: The interference beat is a human-made measurement technique and conceptual map of wave interference. When two coherent waves of frequencies f1 and f2 (with a small difference) superpose, the resultant amplitude varies periodically at the beat frequency |f1 − f2|, producing a regular swelling and fading — beating — of intensity that a listener or detector perceives. The natural interference is the territory; the construct is the human-authored map that names it, quantifies it, and exploits it. Parameters: (1) two superposed waves whose frequencies differ slightly; (2) the beat frequency — the amplitude-modulation rate |f1 − f2|, which directly reveals the difference between the two sources; (3) the exploitation — driving the beat frequency to zero to tune one source to another, or measuring an unknown frequency against a known reference by counting beats. Persistence mechanism: the technique persists through its invariant mathematical relation (beat frequency = |f1 − f2|), its standard use in instrument tuning, heterodyning, and frequency comparison, and its standing as a worked example in physics pedagogy across acoustics, optics, and radio. Distinct from the musical beat, which is the rhythmic temporal unit that organizes meter and serves rhythm — a pulse of emphasis, not an interference measure; the two share only a homographic name. [formal: pulsus interferentiae | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.name: decibel
payload.scope: A human-made logarithmic unit of ratio, invented at Bell Telephone Laboratories in the 1920s to make telephone line performance comparable across long chains of equipment, built to persist through international standardization and universal engineering specification notation.

payload.name: decibel
payload.scope: A human-made logarithmic unit of ratio, invented at Bell Telephone Laboratories in the 1920s to make telephone line performance comparable across long chains of equipment, built to persist through international standardization and universal engineering specification notation.

payload.body: The decibel is a human-made logarithmic unit for expressing the ratio between two values of a physical quantity — power or field amplitude — as a level. Parameters: (1) ratio kind — a power ratio, expressed 10·log10(P1/P0), or a field-amplitude ratio, expressed 20·log10(A1/A0) for voltage, sound pressure, and wave amplitudes, the factor of two following from power being proportional to the square of the field quantity; (2) scale — one decibel is one-tenth of a bel, the whole-logarithm ratio named for Alexander Graham Bell, so a 3 dB step is a doubling of power (a factor of about 2 in field amplitude); (3) reference convention — either the pure relative ratio (dB) or a ratio referenced to a fixed absolute unit, each carried by its own suffix: dBm to 1 mW, dB SPL to 20 µPa, dBV to 1 V, dBu to 0.775 V. Persistence mechanism: the unit persists through international standardization (ITU-R BT.568, IEC 60027), through its standing in the calibration, measurement, and specification practice of acoustics, radio, audio, fiber optics, and electronics, and because it converts the multiplicative factors of cascaded stages into additive levels — which is what carries dynamic range, signal-to-noise ratio, and gain in engineering documents. Distinct from a plain ratio (a linear two-term quotient needing no named unit) and from the logarithm (the mathematical function it applies to a ratio): the decibel is the named unit with a fixed scale (one-tenth of the bel), a quantity-kind convention, and a reference convention. [formal: decima bel | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.name: heterodyning
payload.scope: A human-made frequency-conversion technique in which two signals are deliberately mixed to produce sum and difference frequencies, built to persist as the standard architecture of superheterodyne receivers, spectrum analyzers, and communication systems.

payload.name: heterodyning
payload.scope: A human-made frequency-conversion technique in which two signals are deliberately mixed to produce sum and difference frequencies, built to persist as the standard architecture of superheterodyne receivers, spectrum analyzers, and communication systems.

payload.body: Heterodyning is a human-made frequency-conversion technique: two signals of different frequencies are combined in a nonlinear mixing element — a diode, a transistor, or the auditory system itself — so the output contains the sum (f1 + f2) and the difference (|f1 − f2|) frequencies, and the difference is selected to shift a signal to a more convenient band. Parameters: (1) input pair — a signal at f1 and a local oscillator at f2, chosen so the difference lands the converted signal at a fixed intermediate frequency; (2) mixing element — a nonlinearity whose response generates the sum and difference products; (3) selection — a filter retaining the desired product (normally the difference) and rejecting the sum, the unconverted inputs, and the image frequency f_image = f_IF ± f_LO. Persistence mechanism: it persists as the standard architecture of the superheterodyne receiver — the dominant radio-reception scheme since Edwin Armstrong's 1918 patent — of spectrum analyzers, of FM broadcast transmission, and of communication systems that move signals to a fixed intermediate frequency for gain and filtering; through that engineering standardization, its patent lineage, and its standing as a named technique in electronics pedagogy. Distinct from the interference beat (which names and quantifies the naturally occurring difference tone of two close frequencies for tuning and comparison, without driving a conversion) and from modulation (which loads information onto a carrier rather than shifting a signal's band for processing): in heterodyning the product frequencies are the mechanism, not the message. [formal: mixtura heterodonica | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.scope: A human-made research category of cognitive science: a recurring, nameable pattern of mental operation isolated as an object of study, built to persist as a unit of measurement and instruction across research programs, journals, and curricula.

payload.body: A cognitive phenomenon is a recurring, nameable pattern of mental operation that cognitive science isolates as an object of study — a regularity in perception, memory, reasoning, attention, or learning that can be elicited under controlled conditions and measured across individuals and groups. Parameters: (1) it is a pattern rather than a single event — it recurs across trials, individuals, or populations; (2) it is nameable and distinguishable — the research community tracks it under a stable label with characteristic task batteries or operational signatures (e.g., priming tasks, transfer paradigms, interference effects); (3) it is measurable — an operational signature (reaction-time difference, error-rate difference, performance gap between contexts) separates it from baseline. It persists through research programs (replication, meta-analysis, longitudinal study), institutional practice (journals, conferences, and funding categories organized around named phenomena), and pedagogical transmission (textbooks and curricula that enumerate and teach them). The entry names the made category — the phenomenon-as-studied — not the underlying natural process; that boundary is the map's. [formal: phenomenon cognitivum | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made musical framework — an ordered set of pitch classes spanning an octave, arranged by a fixed interval pattern — built to persist as a teachable, notatable, and performable convention of tonal practice, carried across centuries in notation, pedagogy, and performance.

payload.body: A musical-scale is a human-made ordered set of pitch classes spanning an octave, arranged according to a fixed interval pattern that distinguishes one scale from another (major, minor, pentatonic, chromatic, whole-tone, or a culture-specific pattern). PARAMETERS: (1) pitch-class content — which of the octave's pitch classes are members; (2) interval pattern — the ordered sequence of whole steps, half steps, or other ratios between adjacent members, which gives the scale its identity and separates it from any other collection of the same notes; (3) ordering and octave equivalence — the cyclic arrangement of members and the convention that each pitch class repeats at the octave. It persists as a teachable, notatable, and performable convention: the pattern is carried in notation, pedagogy, and sustained practice, and is re-instantiated in every melody, harmony, and improvisation built on it. [formal: scala musicalis | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made musical convention for fixing the speed of a piece: the rate-of-beat convention carried by metronome marks, Italian tempo names, and the practice of performance, built to persist as the parameter by which a performed beat is timed.

payload.note: Law 8b removal test on the pinned senses per both accepted definitions: tempo is carved as 'the measured speed or rate at which a musical composition or passage is performed, conventionally quantified in beats per minute,' its parameter (1) being 'the speed of the underlying pulse or beat.' beat is carved as 'a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis in time, the temporal unit that organizes rhythmic experience.' Remove beat now: tempo stops OPERATING — BPM has no pulse to count, the metronome mark (quarter note = N) loses the beat unit it designates, and the Italian tempo names, which name speed regions of the pulse, lose their referent. Not a naming loss (the Law 8b objection): the measured quantity itself disappears. Reverse test: beat operates fully without tempo — unmarked pulses, free rhythm, and rubato performance all operate without any fixed speed. Board precedent: meter DEPENDS_ON beat is ACCEPTED — a framework depending on the unit it measures; tempo is the RATE of that same unit, so this is the same accepted pattern, not a leap. The accepted tempo DEPENDS_ON rhythm is complementary, not subsuming: rhythm organizes events into pattern; tempo fixes the speed of the beat itself; no nearer rung (pulse, beat-unit) exists on the board. Pinned sense: tempo as the rate of beats; beat as the temporal unit whose rate tempo fixes.

payload.body: The bel is the human-made whole-logarithm ratio unit: the level corresponding to one power of ten of a power ratio, L = log10(P1/P0) bels. Parameters: (1) ratio kind — for a power ratio, one bel is log10(P1/P0); for a field-amplitude ratio (voltage, sound pressure, wave amplitude), one bel is log10(A1^2/A0^2) = 2·log10(A1/A0), the factor of two following from power being proportional to the square of the field quantity; (2) scale relation to the decibel — 1 bel = 10 decibels: the decibel is the one-tenth subdivision that stuck in practice because a 10:1 power step is too coarse for telephone gain/loss work, so the decibel inherits the bel's logarithmic scale at one-tenth size; (3) natural-log counterpart — the neper (1 Np = ln of the ratio) plays the same role for natural logarithms, with 1 Np ≈ 8.686 dB for field-amplitude ratios. Persistence mechanism: the bel persists as the scale-constant of the decibel (every decibel value is a fraction of a bel), as the named whole-log unit in the literature of logarithmic transmission, and through the standardization of the bel–decibel relation (1 B = 10 dB) in the ITU/IEC system of units. Distinct from the decibel (its one-tenth subdivision, the practical working unit), from the neper (the natural-log counterpart with a different base), and from a plain ratio (a linear two-term quotient needing no logarithmic name). [formal: bel | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: The neper is the human-made natural-logarithm ratio unit: the level corresponding to one natural-logarithm unit of a ratio, L = ln(P1/P0) nepers. Parameters: (1) ratio kind — a power ratio, expressed ln(P1/P0), or a field-amplitude ratio (voltage, sound pressure, wave amplitude), expressed 2·ln(A1/A0) = ln(A1²/A0²), the factor of two following from power being proportional to the square of the field quantity, so that the neper value is the same under either expression, exactly as the decibel value is the same under 10·log10(P1/P0) and 20·log10(A1/A0); (2) scale relation — one neper corresponds to the power ratio e, the base of the natural logarithm (i.e., to the field-amplitude ratio √e), and converts to the base-10 scale by the fixed factor 1 Np = 10·log10(e) dB ≈ 4.3429 dB, while 1 bel = ln(10) Np ≈ 2.3026 Np; (3) base distinction — where the bel and the decibel apply the base-10 logarithm to the ratio, the neper applies the natural logarithm (base e), so the two families measure the same ratio on different logarithmic scales, with a fixed conversion factor of ln(10) ≈ 2.3026 between them. Persistence mechanism: the neper persists as a named non-SI unit in the IEC system of units (IEC 60027), in the literature of logarithmic transmission and in radio, audio, and control engineering where the natural logarithm is native, and through the fixed conversion constants (1 Np ≈ 4.3429 dB, 1 B ≈ 2.3026 Np) that appear in the standards and the textbooks. Distinct from the decibel (the base-10 practical working unit), from the bel (its base-10 whole-log counterpart), from the natural logarithm (the mathematical function the unit applies to a ratio), and from a plain ratio (a linear two-term quotient needing no logarithmic name). [formal: neper | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

payload.body: The tonic is the central pitch of a tonal system: scale degree 1, the 'home' note around which a key is organized. It is the pitch of greatest stability and rest — the goal of cadential motion and the anchor of tonal gravity — from which melody and harmony depart and to which they return. Parameters: (1) scale-degree status — the tonic is degree 1 of the key's scale, the root from which the scale and its intervals are reckoned; (2) functional role — it is the point of rest, resolution, and greatest consonance, the target toward which leading-tone and dominant motion gravitate; (3) relational definition — the tonic is defined relative to the key (the tonic of C major is C) and, reciprocally, the key is defined by its tonic, so the two constitute each other. Persistence mechanism: codified in Western tonal and harmonic theory, taught in music-theory and ear-training curricula (scale-degree numbering, Roman-numeral and functional analysis), reproduced in composition and analysis practice (identifying the tonic by its gravitational pull, its role in cadences, and its position in the key signature), and maintained through the conventions of tonal notation. It is distinguished from the dominant (scale degree 5 — the point of greatest tension that pulls back to the tonic, not the point of rest), from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis; the tonic is a pitch bearing a specific functional role), and from pitch-class (the abstract equivalence class of octave-equivalent pitches; the tonic is the functionally designated one). [formal: tonicus | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: The dominant is scale degree 5 of a key: the pitch a perfect fifth above the tonic, and the bearer of the dominant function — the point of greatest harmonic tension in a tonal system, whose resolution back to the tonic is the basic engine of tonal motion. Parameters: (1) intervallic status — the dominant is the fifth degree of the key's scale, a perfect fifth above the tonic (in C major, G); (2) functional role — it is the point of greatest tension, the degree and chord that pull back to the tonic, the target of cadential motion and the source of the dominant–tonic pull that organizes phrase structure; (3) relational definition — the dominant is defined relative to the key and tonic (the dominant of C major is G), and reciprocally fixes the key's tension structure, so the two constitute each other the way tonic and key do. Persistence mechanism: codified in Western tonal and harmonic theory, taught in music-theory and ear-training curricula (functional harmony; Roman-numeral analysis, where V denotes the dominant), reproduced in composition and analysis practice (cadential analysis, the tonic–dominant alternation as the cell of tonal motion), and maintained through the conventions of tonal notation. It is distinguished from the tonic (scale degree 1 — the point of REST to which the dominant resolves, not the point of tension), from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis; the dominant is a pitch bearing a specific functional role), and from the dominant chord (the triad built on the fifth degree — a chord built ON the dominant, not the degree and function itself). [formal: dominantis | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: The leading tone is scale degree 7 of a major key — the pitch a semitone below the tonic — and the bearer of the leading function: the point of strongest upward pull, whose half-step resolution to the tonic is the sharpest edge of cadential motion and the voice-leading engine that completes the dominant's pull home. Parameters: (1) intervallic status — in a major key the seventh scale degree sits a semitone (diatonic semitone) below the tonic (in C major, B), and it is this half-step distance that gives it its leading character; the corresponding degree in a natural minor key is a subtonic, a whole tone below the tonic, and does not bear the leading function; (2) functional role — the leading tone is the degree that resolves upward by semitone to the tonic; it appears in the dominant chord as its third (B in a G major triad over C) and supplies the voice-leading urgency that makes the dominant–tonic cadence close; (3) relational definition — the leading tone is defined relative to the tonic (the leading tone of C major is B), and its function is the completion of the dominant's resolution, so it is the dominant's pull expressed at the voice-leading level. Persistence mechanism: codified in Western tonal and voice-leading theory, taught in harmony and counterpoint curricula (scale-degree analysis; the leading-tone–tonic resolution as a basic voice-leading pattern), reproduced in composition and analysis practice (cadence analysis, the leading tone's semitone pull in the final cadence of a phrase), and maintained through the conventions of tonal notation (the raised seventh in minor keys, the harmonic minor, exists to produce the leading tone). It is distinguished from the subtonic (the natural-minor seventh degree, a whole tone below the tonic — same scale position, no half-step, no leading function), from the dominant (the chord/degree to which the leading tone belongs and which it sharpens — the leading tone is the third of the dominant chord, its semitone voice, not the fifth-degree function itself), and from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis; the leading tone is a pitch bearing the specific function of the semitone pull to the tonic). payload.body: A scale-degree is a position within a musical scale: one of the scale's ordered ordinal slots (1-7 in an octave scale, numbered from the tonic) which, once the scale is fixed, holds a named pitch-class. PARAMETERS: (1) ordinal position — the slot's index within the scale's ordered collection, counted from the tonic (1 = tonic, 2 = supertonic, 3 = mediant, 4 = subdominant, 5 = dominant, 6 = submediant, 7 = leading-tone in major / subtonic in natural minor); (2) scale of reference — the particular scale of which the degree is a position; the same ordinal slot holds different pitch-classes in different scales (the fifth degree is G in C major, F# in B major), so a degree is a position, not a pitch; (3) diatonic interval — the interval from the tonic that the slot occupies (the fifth degree sits a perfect fifth above the tonic in a major scale); (4) functional role, in tonal contexts — the cadential pull the position carries (the dominant function of the fifth degree, the leading function of the major seventh degree), which specific named degrees carry as their own entries. PERSISTENCE: codified in tonal theory as scale-degree numerals (1-7), solfege syllables (do-re-mi-fa-sol-la-ti), and degree names; taught in harmony, counterpoint, and ear-training curricula; re-instantiated in every analysis — Roman-numeral analysis names chords by their degree of origin and voice-leading tracks the degrees' motion. Distinctions: from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis — a degree is a position a pitch occupies within a scale, and the same pitch is a different degree in different keys); from a note (a notated or performed event); from the musical scale itself (the ordered collection — the degree is a position within it, not the collection); and from the specific named degrees (dominant, leading-tone — particular kinds of scale-degree filed as their own entries). [formal: gradus scalae | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: The subtonic is scale degree 7 of a natural minor scale: the pitch a whole tone (major second) below the tonic that bears NO leading function. PARAMETERS: (1) intervallic status — the subtonic sits a whole tone (two semitones) below the tonic, in direct contrast to the leading tone, which sits a semitone (one semitone) below the tonic and bears the upward semitone pull; the whole-tone distance is what disqualifies the degree from the leading function (in A minor, G natural is the subtonic, G# the leading tone); (2) scale context — the subtonic is the unaltered seventh degree of the natural minor scale and reappears in the descending form of the melodic minor (which restores the natural minor's lower three degrees), whereas the raised leading tone appears in the ascending melodic minor and in harmonic minor; (3) functional role — as the root of the subtonic triad (vII, a major triad in minor keys, e.g. G major over A minor) it resolves to the tonic by step rather than by semitone pull, and in jazz usage it is the flat-seven (b7) that colors the dominant-seventh and minor-seventh chords. PERSISTENCE: codified in tonal and jazz theory as the natural-minor seventh degree, distinguished in every harmony curriculum from the raised leading tone (harmonic/melodic minor), taught as the b7 in jazz harmony, and maintained in the practice of cadence analysis where the vII-VI-i motion and the absence of the semitone pull mark the subtonic. Distinctions: from the leading tone (same ordinal slot — degree 7 — but a semitone below the tonic with the upward semitone pull; the two are alternate occupants of the seventh degree, filed as separate entries); from a bare pitch (any point on the pitch axis — the subtonic is a degree bearing a specific whole-tone-below-tonic status and the absence of the leading function); from the dominant (degree 5 and its cadential function — a different ordinal slot entirely). Law 8b removal test on the generic construct passes. A scale-degree's entire mechanism is indexing the scale's ordered pitch-class collection: the degree number is a slot number counted from the tonic within a fixed ordered set. Remove the musical-scale construct and the index has nothing to index — 'the fifth degree' without an ordered collection is a label with no position to name, and the construct stops operating. It is not merely sayable in the scale's absence; it ceases to function. Same shape as the accepted meter-DEP-beat and chord-DEP-interval dependencies: a construct that operates by counting the ordered units of a larger whole depends on that whole.

The pinned sense is 'the dominant as the fifth scale degree', but the dominant's mechanism is not indexing the scale — it is the intervallic and functional relation to the tonic: the pitch a perfect fifth above the tonic that carries the key's greatest tension, the engine of cadential motion. Remove the musical-scale construct and the coordinate label 'degree 5' loses its frame, but the dominant still OPERATES: the perfect-fifth relation to the tonic is defined by pitch and interval, and the tension-to-rest function it carries is the voice-leading core of tonal motion. The ordinal slot is where the dominant sits, not what it runs on — the scale dependency belongs to the slot itself (scale-degree DEPENDS_ON musical-scale), and the dominant's real dependency is already on the board: dominant DEPENDS_ON tonic, accepted. Location is not mechanism; the note's ordinal appeal is identity (it is a degree) and naming (the scale calls it that), not a removal consequence.

Law 8b removal test fails, and the accepted record already shows where the real dependency sits. The image-frequency's mechanism is the mixing symmetry f_image = f_LO +/- f_IF — the mirror of the desired signal about the local oscillator. Remove the sideband construct and the image still exists and still causes the superheterodyne image problem: any frequency on the mirror side of the LO that falls in the front-end passband still converts to the IF. The pinned sense itself mis-carves the phenomenon: 'the unwanted frequency that produces the same intermediate frequency' — the image is an INPUT frequency, not a spectral band produced by modulation; it yields an undesired output at the IF, not an undesired sideband. The board's accepted record files the correct dependency: image-frequency DEPENDS_ON heterodyning and DERIVED_FROM heterodyning, both accepted — the mixing operation is the substrate whose removal actually stops the image operating.

For whose sake: modulation is maintained as a core operation of the signal-processing craft. Under Law 11c's mass sense the claim holds: modulation is built and maintained for the signal-processing craft the way its accepted sibling edges hold. The note is thin, but the pinned claim is the accepted pattern on this board.

payload.note: Law 8b removal test, pinned sense: the neper as the natural-logarithm ratio unit whose value is L = ln(P1/P0). The neper's entire mechanism is applying the natural logarithm to a ratio — its value IS a logarithm. Remove the logarithm construct and there is no ln by which to compute the level from the ratio; the named unit has no operating content left (a plain ratio is exactly what its own definition distinguishes it from). The parallel decibel-DEPENDS_ON-logarithm claim stands on the identical test (its value is 10*log10 of the ratio). The log is the mechanism, not merely the origin: the origin is already recorded separately (neper DERIVED_FROM logarithm, accepted), mirroring image-frequency's dual accepted edges to heterodyning.
